scenes.name: La prensa musical de 1966
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: La fuente principal del libro. Nada en Estados Unidos se comparaba a los cuatro semanarios británicos (New Musical Express, Melody Maker, Record Mirror y Disc and Music Echo) ni a la revista Rave, que cubrieron el año casi al detalle; las revistas pop americanas como 16 o TeenSet eran mensuales y no podían seguir el ritmo, salvo el semanario KRLA Beat de Los Ángeles. Penny Valentine, Tony Hall y Derek Taylor definieron el año, y en las columnas de Ralph J. Gleason en el San Francisco Chronicle y en las revistas que nacieron en 1966 (Crawdaddy!, Mojo Navigator, The Oracle, Heatwave, International Times) ya estaban todas las ideas de lo que quedaba de década: la generación del amor, la oposición a Vietnam, la crítica del consumismo juvenil, una sociedad alternativa. Comentaristas veteranos como Robert Shelton («Orpheus Plugs In»), Nat Hentoff o Kenneth Allsop vieron que algo extraordinario pasaba en la cultura juvenil.

podcast.title: "We've Only Just Begun" Origin (1970)
podcast.body: As a journeyman songwriter, Paul Williams co-wrote "We've Only Just Begun" and sang the jingle for a Crocker Citizens Bank commercial. This exposure caught the ear of Richard Carpenter, leading to The Carpenters' hugely successful rendition and the song's transformation into a pop classic. "The Jingle was sung by the man who co-wrote it, Journeyman Songwriter Paul Williams."

podcast.title: Phantom of the Paradise (1974) - Music and Acting
podcast.body: In 1974, Paul Williams was hired by director Brian De Palma to star in and write the music for 'Phantom of the Paradise,' a rock musical horror comedy loosely based on 'The Phantom of the Opera,' where he played the evil character Swan. "In 1974, he was hired by director Brian De Palma to start in and write the music for Phantom of the Paradise, a strange rock musical horror comedy loosely based on the Phantom of the Opera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Phantom of the Paradise – Actor and Composer (1974)
podcast.body: In 1974, Paul Williams was hired by director Brian De Palma to star in and write the music for "Phantom of the Paradise," a rock musical horror comedy loosely based on "The Phantom of the Opera." He played the villain, Swan, whose music venue is terrorized by the disfigured Winslow Leech. The film was a box office flop globally, except for its bizarre and enduring popularity in Winnipeg.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Potential Proto-Goth/Death Metal Inventor (1974)
podcast.body: Paul Williams' work in "Phantom of the Paradise" in 1974, particularly the "Rock Opera" within the film and the fictional band The Undead (whose singer, Peter Ebling, wore corpse paint similar to modern death/black metal), leads to a theory that he accidentally invented proto-goth or proto-death metal music. Goth music didn't widely emerge until bands like Bauhaus in the late 1970s, and death metal in the mid-1980s.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Additional Verses for Freddie Allen
podcast.body: Williams and his songwriting partner had penned a bridge and a third verse for a version of "We've Only Just Begun" that was recorded by an artist named Freddie Allen. However, Allen's version of the song ultimately did not achieve hit status. "As it turned out, Williams and his songwriting partner had penned a bridge and a third verse for a version of the song recorded by one Freddie Allen."

podcast.title: Career-Breaking Song
podcast.body: Paul Williams personally credits "We've Only Just Begun" with being the pivotal song that broke his career, bringing him significant recognition and opening new doors in the music industry due to its widespread success. "Paul Williams credits the song with Breaking His Career."

podcast.title: Proto-Goth/Death Metal Theory
podcast.body: A theory suggests that Paul Williams, through his work on the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' may have accidentally invented goth or death metal music, preceding their recognized emergence in the late 1970s and mid-1980s, respectively. "Can we say that Paul Williams, the guy who wrote songs for the muppets, accidentally invented both?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Swan Character in Phantom of the Paradise
podcast.body: Paul Williams played the villainous character Swan in Brian De Palma's 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' an evil figure who steals Winslow Leech's music and operates "The Paradise" music venue. "It tells the story of poor Winslow Leech whose music is stolen by the evil Swan. That's Paul Williams character."
